thread.title: Apple: BMO Cuts to Hold; The End of iPhone Price Increases

author: Barron's
title: Apple: BMO Cuts to Hold; The End of iPhone Price Increases

organizations.name: tim long of bmo capital markets

text:
It's just 40 hours till Apple ( AAPL ) reports results on Thursday afternoon, after the closing bell, but a good time to reassess the stock, according to Tim Long of BMO Capital Markets , who this morning cut his rating on the stock to Market Perform from Outperform, after cutting estimates for the March quarter outlook both for iPhone units and prices.
"We expect a meaningful guide lower when the company reports on Thursday night, on the order of $5-6 billion compared to consensus revenue estimates," he writes. His current estimate is for revenue of $39.9 billion in March, versus his prior $46 billion and the consensus $45.57 billion.
Acknowledging "there has been much in the press" about cuts to iPhone, Long writes that he is "more concerned by a secular change for iPhone," that change being that "following 10 years where ASPs have generally moved higher, we believe prices will plateau as with the rest of the industry."
Apple has done a good job of moving ASPs higher despite others in the industry flat-lining. We estimate that about 30% of iPhones will be priced over $900 this year, but we do not expect this figure to go any higher, particularly as only 12% of smartphones globally sell for over $600.
Long's estimate for March units goes to 55 million from his prior 63 million, and below the consensus for 59.3 million. His average price for iPhone goes to $726 from a prior $732, and below consensus for $756.
And, there's no 10-year iPhone up next , he contends:
We still view the iPhone base as growing, and the devices are on average getting older. However, without a compelling product cycle in September, we may see a slow upgrade cycle once again. The recent stock reaction reminds us of early 2016, but later that year many investors started looking towards OLED and the 10-year anniversary phone, which drove the stock higher. No such product is on the horizon now.
In addition, "We expect no growth year over year in the China market, a reversal from last quarter's 12% growth," writes Long. "We believe China sales will be about flat in December, with units down 9% year/year."
For the full fiscal year ending in September, Long cuts his estimates to $161 billion in revenue and $10.46 in earnings, down from a prior $176.88 billion and $11.34. That's assuming 227 million iPhone sold, versus this prior estimate for 246 million, and consensus for 236.5 million.
For 2019 , he expects $162.2 billion in revenue and $11.92 per share, down from $179.2 billion and $12.27 previously. That's assuming sales of the same 227 million units, versus what he thought might be 249 million units. Consensus for 2019 stands at 240 million units.
Apple shares on Tuesday closed at $166.97, down 99 cents.
